# Visualizing Amounts

## Bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical data


:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-bad", fig_bar_bad(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Order matters (ascending or descending)
- Horizontal bars 
    - Often allow for longer labels
    - Fit better on standard pages
    - Worse on standard slides 


:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-good", fig_bar_good(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Grouped bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical-by-categorical data
- Order matters (ascending or descending)
- Grouping matters - Bars you want to compare should be adjacent

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-grouped", fig_bar_grouped(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Dot plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical data
- Use when you do not want an axis to start at zero
- Order still matters

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-dot", fig_dot(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 1.4, width = 5)
place_fig("fig-bar-long", fig_bar_long(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 5, width = 5)
```

## Heatmaps

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical-by-categorical data
- Map continuous values to color not position
- Best when there are many groups in each category and you are implying broad trends not precise values
- Order still matters
- Use sequential or diverging color scales that are colorblind safe

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-heatmap", fig_heatmap(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```
